metadata.baselayout_description: Three-layer spatial portfolio rebuilt for performance. {{projects.ashwingupta-dev.metrics.imageReduction}} image reduction, {{projects.ashwingupta-dev.metrics.javascriptReduction}} JS cut, {{projects.ashwingupta-dev.metrics.animatedNodesEliminated}} animated DOM nodes eliminated, stable 60fps under CPU throttle.

blocks.ashwingupta_dev_th_subtitle: A portfolio site is its own proof unit. The original claimed performance engineering while shipping every symptom of the opposite. Rebuilt end-to-end, then extended with an ambient interface system that treats the chrome as part of the argument.
blocks.the_problem_with_self_defeating_baseline: The designer baseline shipped 400 CSS-animated DOM particles, a 2 MB JPEG hero, Google Fonts loaded per-component, and 72 unvetted dependencies. Every technical visitor's first data point was a performance failure on the site claiming performance engineering. The standard response - clean it up, swap some images - doesn't address the structural problem. The site needed to signal systems thinking, and it was doing the opposite at the source.
blocks.the_architecture_th_body: Rebuilt end-to-end as a three-layer spatial interface: environment shell, Canvas 2D particle field, hologram surface. All visual effects collapsed into a single Canvas RAF loop, eliminating {{projects.ashwingupta-dev.metrics.animatedNodesEliminated}} CSS-animated DOM nodes entirely. Images converted to WebP with
blocks.the_architecture_th_body_2: preload on the hero. Below-fold sections split via React.lazy and Suspense so the initial bundle only contains what the first viewport needs.
blocks.the_architecture_th_body_3: Scanline texture pre-rendered to an offscreen canvas - 1 drawImage per frame instead of 270 fillRect calls. Edge cache rebuilt every 3 frames. RAF paused on visibility change. Mouse tracking gated behind RAF. Each technique eliminates work at the source rather than hiding it. Optimization is structural, not cosmetic.
blocks.the_ambient_interface_system_th_body: After the performance baseline was locked in, the portfolio grew an ambient HUD layer - persistent fixed widgets that add spatial context without intruding on content.
blocks.the_ambient_interface_system_th_body_2: Bottom-left: a geolocation widget that resolves the visitor's coordinates via
blocks.the_ambient_interface_system_th_body_4: timezone if permission is denied - to the nearest IATA airport code using
blocks.the_ambient_interface_system_th_body_5: across a curated set of major airports worldwide. Paired with a live clock and GMT offset display for both the visitor's location and home ({{profile.homeAirport}}).
blocks.the_ambient_interface_system_th_body_7: viewport coordinates, a session elapsed timer, and a radial SVG progress arc for back-to-top navigation. The arc tracks scroll position per-page, resets cleanly on Astro View Transitions via

blocks.the_ambient_interface_system_th_body_12: across Astro's View Transitions - they survive page navigation without remounting, without state bleed from the previous page, and without a single frame of flicker.
blocks.the_exploration_tracker_th_body: A progress widget embedded in the right HUD that measures how much of the site a visitor has actually read - not binary page visits, but
blocks.the_exploration_tracker_th_body_2: per page. Of the 17 distinct content pages tracked, each contributes proportionally based on the maximum scroll depth reached during the visit. Arriving at a page and leaving immediately contributes near zero. Scrolling to the bottom gives full credit for that page's 1/18 share of the total.
